news.title: Motivated De Bruyne wants to keep playing for Belgium
news.lede: Sept 22 - Belgium midfielder Kevin De Bruyne will continue to play international football as long as he remains motivated, saying he had not considered quitting the team after the World Cup despite being the last of the country's golden generation. De Bruyne, 35, has won 124 caps since his debut as a teenager in 2010 under Georges Leekens and is lined up to add more appearances as Belgium now have Mark van Bommel in charge. The new era begins against Italy in Rome on Friday, followed by Nations League clashes with France (twice) and Turkey over the next three weeks. In recent weeks, De Bruyne has seen long-time colleague Axel Witsel retire and goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois sit out the Nations League but told reporters on Tuesday he had never considered quitting the national team.

news.title: ‘Be less sh*t’ - Jurgen Klopp set simple challenge as Germany boss as ex-Liverpool manager is backed to bring ‘heavy metal football’ to the Euros & World Cup
news.lede: Jurgen Klopp has been set the simple challenge of being “less sh*t” as he prepares to embark on a new challenge as manager of the Germany national team. Robert Huth has told GOAL that the former Borussia Dortmund and Liverpool boss will bring “heavy metal football” to the international arena while chasing down European Championship and World Cup crowns. Klopp stepped away from the stresses of coaching during the summer of 2024 when bringing an iconic nine-year stint at Anfield to a close. He had delivered Premier League and Champions League titles to Merseyside.

news.title: Real Madrid star Jude Bellingham reignites World Cup feud - 'You don't talk without Messi'
news.lede: Jude Bellingham and Cristian Romero clashed during the Madrid derby at the weekend as the opposing players reignited their World Cup feud. Atletico Madrid got the better of Jose Mourinho and Real Madrid in an ill-tempered affair, which saw Bellingham and the former Tottenham defender clash and the match end 2-1. The duo were seen exchanging words through the match at the Metropolitano, with their World Cup semi-final clash clearly still fresh in the memory. England took the lead that night before the South Americans rallied late on, scoring their winner in stoppage time.

news.title: Fifa reform claims questioned by FAW chief Noel Mooney
news.lede: Gianni Infantino succeeded Sepp Blatter as Fifa president in 2016. Football Association of Wales chief executive Noel Mooney has played down suggestions Fifa is planning major reforms. Fifa president Gianni Infantino has proposed an external review of how world football's governing body operates and says he is open to reform. In a letter sent to members of the Fifa Council and all of its national associations, Infantino explains the independent process would "recommend potential improvements".

news.title: South American International Preview: Messi Era Ends As New Eras Begin After 2026 World Cup
news.lede: The first international window since the 2026 World Cup is upon us, with all ten CONMEBOL sides set to take part. Many countries have opted to play their matches away from home, while some will remain in South America. It promises to be an intriguing window, even though there is no competitive action. It gives managers a fresh opportunity to experiment with new ideas and players as preparations begin for the 2028 Copa América and the 2030 World Cup qualifiers.

news.title: The president of the German federation exposes Infantino: his message is an "obvious trick" to stay in power
news.lede: Less than 24 hours after Gianni Infantino's conciliatory message, the FIFA president found the fiercest response coming from within his own house. Bernd Neuendorf, president of the German Football Association and a member of the FIFA Council, detonated a resounding bombshell. He dismissed the FIFA president's move as no reform but a "blatant electoral ploy", declaring that the Swiss had completely lost his credibility and was no longer the right man to lead the game. Infantino had written to all 211 member nations this week, proposing talks on reform within world football's governing body in a bid to contain the ongoing crisis.
